title: Making a Complaint
summary: A customer calls a hotel to complain about a noisy room and asks for a solution.
description: An intermediate phone-conversation focused on polite-but-firm complaints and problem resolution. Vocabulary includes 'apologise', 'refund', 'compensation', and 'manager'.

vocabulary.definition: a statement that you are unhappy about something
to say you are sorry for something you have done wrong
money that is returned to you because you are not satisfied
something, usually money, given to make up for a problem
to find a solution to a problem

dialogue.text: Good evening. This is the Lake View Hotel. How can I help you?
Good evening. I am calling to make a complaint about room 312.
I am very sorry to hear that. Can you tell me what happened?
The room was extremely noisy because of construction work next door, even at midnight.
I sincerely apologise for that. That is not the experience we want for our guests.
I appreciate that. What kind of compensation can you offer?
We can offer you a full refund for last night and a free dinner tonight.
That is fair. Can I also move to a quieter room for the rest of my stay?
Of course. I will move you to a room on the top floor, away from the street.
Thank you. I am happy with this solution.

questions.q: What compensation does the hotel offer?
options: A refund and a free dinner
A discount on the next visit

questions.q: Where will the customer be moved?
options: To a room on the ground floor
To a room on the top floor

trueFalse.statement: The construction work happened only during the day.
trueFalse.explanation: The customer says the noise was 'even at midnight,' so it was happening at night too.
The receptionist says 'I sincerely apologise for that.'

teacherTips: Pre-teach the contrast between polite and rude complaints. Use the dialogue as the polite model.
Drill formulaic phrases: 'I am calling to make a complaint…', 'I appreciate that…', 'I am happy with…'
After listening, students write a short formal complaint email about a real situation (school, café, gym).

es.title: Presentar una queja
es.summary: Un cliente llama a un hotel para quejarse de una habitación ruidosa y pide una solución.
es.description: Una conversación telefónica intermedia centrada en quejas educadas pero firmes y en la resolución de problemas. El vocabulario incluye 'apologise', 'refund', 'compensation' y 'manager'.

vocabulary.definition: una declaración de que no estás contento con algo
decir que sientes haber hecho algo mal
dinero que se te devuelve porque no estás satisfecho
algo, normalmente dinero, que se da para compensar un problema
encontrar una solución a un problema

options: Un reembolso y una cena gratis
Un descuento en la próxima visita
A una habitación en la planta baja
A una habitación en la última planta

trueFalse.statement: Las obras solo ocurrían durante el día.
trueFalse.explanation: El cliente dice que el ruido era 'even at midnight', así que también ocurría por la noche.

trueFalse.statement: El hotel se niega a disculparse.
trueFalse.explanation: El recepcionista dice 'I sincerely apologise for that'.

teacherTips: Enseña el contraste entre quejas educadas y groseras. Usa el diálogo como modelo educado.
Practica fórmulas fijas: 'I am calling to make a complaint…', 'I appreciate that…', 'I am happy with…'.
Después de escuchar, los estudiantes escriben un correo formal corto de queja sobre una situación real (escuela, cafetería, gimnasio).
